+\section{The source assertion}
+
+The Magic Square game $\game^{\MS}$ of \cite[Section~7]{Ji2020MIPStar} has nine
+variables $x_1,\ldots,x_9$ over $\F_2$ in a $3\times 3$ grid and six parity
+constraints, one per row and column.  Its verifier samples a uniformly random
+edge $\Constraint_i \,\text{---}\, \Variable_j$ of the bipartite incidence
+graph and sends one endpoint to a uniformly random player and the other
+endpoint to the other player.  The constraint player answers with an
+assignment to the three variables of its constraint, the variable player with
+one bit, and the players win when the assignment satisfies the constraint and
+the two reported values of $x_j$ agree.  Two features are used below: the game
+is \emph{role-symmetric}, so each player is asked constraint questions and
+variable questions, and its question distribution is supported on
+constraint--variable pairs, so the same question is never sent to both
+players.
+
+A strategy $\strategy = (\ket{\psi}, A, B)$ consists of a unit vector
+$\ket{\psi} \in \mH_{\mathrm A} \ot \mH_{\mathrm B}$ and POVMs $\{A^x_a\}$,
+$\{B^y_b\}$; $\val^*(\game^{\MS},\strategy)$ is the acceptance probability.
+The strategy is \emph{symmetric} when $\mH_{\mathrm A} = \mH_{\mathrm B}$,
+$\ket{\psi}$ is invariant under exchanging the two factors, and $A = B$; the
+source writes such a strategy $\strategy = (\ket{\psi}, M)$ and states that it
+almost always restricts attention to this class.%
+\footnote{Definitions and the convention:
+\path{references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex}, lines~74--92
+and~174.  In this repository: \path{def:symmetric-game} in
+\path{blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex}, formalized as
+\leanid{MIPStarRE.QPBT.SymmetricStrategy}.}
+For operators $M, N$ and a state $\ket{\varphi}$ we write
+$M \approx_\zeta N$ for
+$\bra{\varphi}(M-N)^\dagger(M-N)\ket{\varphi} \le O(\zeta)$, and for POVM
+families $\{M_a\}, \{N_a\}$ for
+$\sum_a \bra{\varphi}(M_a-N_a)^\dagger(M_a-N_a)\ket{\varphi} \le O(\zeta)$;
+the state is named wherever the relation is used.
+
+The rigidity theorem asserts:%
+\footnote{Statement and proof at
+\path{references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex},
+lines~620--652; the blueprint statement is \path{thm:ms-rigidity} in
+\path{blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex}, now in the corrected form.
+Tracked in \ghissue{172}; the refutation is recorded on \ghissue{105}, and the
+decisions to record and to repair the statement are items~B4 and~B5 on
+\ghissue{26}.}
+if $\strategy = (\ket{\psi},A,B)$ succeeds in $\game^{\MS}$ with probability
+$1-\eps$, then there are local isometries
+$\phi_{\mathrm A} \colon \mH_{\mathrm A} \to \mH_{\mathrm A'} \ot
+\mH_{\mathrm A''}$ and
+$\phi_{\mathrm B} \colon \mH_{\mathrm B} \to \mH_{\mathrm B'} \ot
+\mH_{\mathrm B''}$ with
+$\mH_{\mathrm A'}, \mH_{\mathrm B'} \cong (\C^2)^{\ot 2}$, and a state
+$\ket{\aux} \in \mH_{\mathrm A''} \ot \mH_{\mathrm B''}$, such that
+\begin{equation}
+  \bigl\| \phi_{\mathrm A} \ot \phi_{\mathrm B}\ket{\psi}
+    - \ket{\EPR_2}^{\ot 2} \ot \ket{\aux} \bigr\| \le O(\sqrt\eps)
+  \tag{\path{thm:ms-rigidity}, 1}
+\end{equation}
+and, writing $\tilde A^x_a = \phi_{\mathrm A} A^x_a \phi_{\mathrm A}^\dagger$
+and $\tilde B^y_b = \phi_{\mathrm B} B^y_b \phi_{\mathrm B}^\dagger$,
+\begin{equation}
+  \tilde A^{\Variable_1}_b \ot \Id \approx_{\sqrt\eps}
+    (\sigma^X_b)_{\mathrm A'} \ot \Id,
+  \qquad
+  \Id \ot \tilde B^{\Variable_1}_b \approx_{\sqrt\eps}
+    \Id \ot (\sigma^X_b)_{\mathrm B'},
+  \tag{\path{thm:ms-rigidity}, 2}
+\end{equation}
+with respect to $\ket{\Theta} = \ket{\EPR_2}^{\ot 2}_{\mathrm{A'B'}} \ot
+\ket{\aux}_{\mathrm{A''B''}}$, together with the two companion relations for
+$\Variable_5$ and $\sigma^Z$ and the anticommutation consequence for the
+associated observables.
+
+\section{What the conclusion forces}
+\label{sec:forces}
+
+Write $O_A = \tilde A^{\Variable_1}_0 - \tilde A^{\Variable_1}_1$ and
+$O_B = \tilde B^{\Variable_1}_0 - \tilde B^{\Variable_1}_1$ for the transported
+$\pm 1$ observables, and $\mathcal O_A, \mathcal O_B$ for the untransported
+ones.  Take $\eps = 0$, so that all the estimates above are exact.  Then
+$\phi_{\mathrm A} \ot \phi_{\mathrm B}\ket{\psi} = \ket{\Theta}$, and since
+$\phi^\dagger \phi = \Id$ for an isometry, $\tilde M \phi = \phi M$ for each
+transported operator, whence
+\begin{equation}
+  \bra{\psi}\,\mathcal O_A \ot \mathcal O_B\,\ket{\psi}
+  = \bra{\Theta}\, O_A \ot O_B \,\ket{\Theta}
+  = \bra{\Theta}\, \sigma^X_{\mathrm A'} \ot \sigma^X_{\mathrm B'}
+    \,\ket{\Theta}
+  = 1 .
+  \label{eq:forced-correlation}
+\end{equation}
+The middle equality uses the exact form of the two relations in
+(\path{thm:ms-rigidity},~2) and the self-adjointness of the observables; the
+last one is the identity
+$\bra{\EPR_2}\, M \ot N \,\ket{\EPR_2} = \tr(M N^{\mathsf T})/2$ applied to
+$M = N = \sigma^X$ on the first extracted qubit pair.  For $\pm 1$ observables,
+$\bra{\psi} \mathcal O_A \ot \mathcal O_B \ket{\psi} = 1$ is equivalent to
+$(\mathcal O_A \ot \Id)\ket{\psi} = (\Id \ot \mathcal O_B)\ket{\psi}$, that is,
+to the two players' $\Variable_1$ measurements agreeing on $\ket{\psi}$.  The
+conclusion of the theorem therefore contains a cross-player agreement
+assertion about a question pair that the game never samples.
+
+\section{A perfect strategy violating the conclusion}
+\label{sec:counterexample}
+
+Fix the canonical Mermin--Peres operator solution on
+$\mathcal K = \C^2 \ot \C^2$: the nine $\pm 1$ observables
+\[
+  \begin{array}{ccc}
+    \sigma^X \ot \Id & \Id \ot \sigma^X & \sigma^X \ot \sigma^X \\
+    \Id \ot \sigma^Z & \sigma^Z \ot \Id & \sigma^Z \ot \sigma^Z \\
+    \sigma^X \ot \sigma^Z & \sigma^Z \ot \sigma^X & \sigma^Y \ot \sigma^Y
+  \end{array}
+\]
+placed in the grid, whose rows and first two columns multiply to $\Id$ and
+whose third column multiplies to $-\Id$.  All nine are real and symmetric.  Let
+$\ket{\Omega} \in \mathcal K \ot \mathcal K$ be the maximally entangled state,
+which is $\ket{\EPR_2}^{\ot 2}$ after reordering the qubits, and let $M$ be the
+measurement family that answers $\Constraint_i$ by jointly measuring the three
+commuting observables of row or column $i$ and answers $\Variable_j$ by the
+two-outcome measurement $\{(\Id \pm O_j)/2\}$.  Then $(\ket{\Omega}, M)$ is a
+symmetric, projective, consistent strategy of value $1$.
+
+Now give each player a copy of $\mathcal K \ot \mathcal K$ and split the two
+roles across the two copies: on a constraint question the first player measures
+copy~$1$ and the second measures copy~$2$, and on a variable question the first
+player measures copy~$2$ and the second measures copy~$1$.  With the state
+$\ket{\Omega}_{\mathrm A_1 \mathrm B_1} \ot
+\ket{\Omega}_{\mathrm A_2 \mathrm B_2}$, every sampled question pair consists of
+one constraint and one variable, so the two measurements actually performed are
+the canonical perfect pair acting on a single maximally entangled copy: on
+copy~$1$ when the first player holds the constraint, and on copy~$2$ when the
+second player does.  The value is therefore $1$.  The two players' $\Variable_1$
+observables, however, act on $\mathrm A_2$ and $\mathrm B_1$, whose joint
+reduced state is a product of maximally mixed states, so
+\begin{equation}
+  \bra{\psi}\,\mathcal O_A \ot \mathcal O_B\,\ket{\psi}
+  = \frac{\tr(\sigma^X \ot \Id)}{4} \cdot \frac{\tr(\sigma^X \ot \Id)}{4}
+  = 0 ,
+  \label{eq:zero-correlation}
+\end{equation}
+contradicting \eqref{eq:forced-correlation}.  The same computation with
+$\sigma^Z$ refutes the $\Variable_5$ relations.  The source statement is thus
+false at $\eps = 0$, and no choice of isometries or auxiliary state can repair
+it, since \eqref{eq:forced-correlation} used only that $\phi_{\mathrm A}$ and
+$\phi_{\mathrm B}$ are isometries.  In the terms of \eqref{eq:defect}, this
+strategy has $\Delta_1 = \Delta_5 = 1$: for $\pm1$ observables
+$\sum_b \|(A_b \ot \Id - \Id \ot B_b)\ket\psi\|^2
+= 1 - \bra\psi \mathcal O_A \ot \mathcal O_B \ket\psi$
+whenever the two measurements are projective on the state.
+
+\section{Symmetry does not repair the statement}
+\label{sec:symmetric}
+
+The strategy just described is not symmetric: the two players use different
+measurement families.  It is natural to hope that the source's standing
+restriction to symmetric strategies excludes it.  It does not.
+
+Give each player a flag qubit and two copies of $\mathcal K$, so that the local
+space is $\C^2 \ot \mathcal K \ot \mathcal K$, and take the state
+\[
+  \ket{\psi} = \frac{1}{\sqrt2}
+    \bigl( \ket{0}_{f_{\mathrm A}}\ket{1}_{f_{\mathrm B}}
+         + \ket{1}_{f_{\mathrm A}}\ket{0}_{f_{\mathrm B}} \bigr)
+    \ot \ket{\Omega}_{\mathrm A_1 \mathrm B_1}
+    \ot \ket{\Omega}_{\mathrm A_2 \mathrm B_2} .
+\]
+Both players use the single family
+\begin{align*}
+  M^{\Constraint_i}_a
+    &= \ket{0}\!\bra{0}_f \ot (M^{\Constraint_i}_a)_1 \ot \Id_2
+     + \ket{1}\!\bra{1}_f \ot \Id_1 \ot (M^{\Constraint_i}_a)_2 , \\
+  M^{\Variable_j}_b
+    &= \ket{0}\!\bra{0}_f \ot \Id_1 \ot (M^{\Variable_j}_b)_2
+     + \ket{1}\!\bra{1}_f \ot (M^{\Variable_j}_b)_1 \ot \Id_2 :
+\end{align*}
+a player whose flag reads $0$ answers constraints from copy~$1$ and variables
+from copy~$2$, and a player whose flag reads $1$ does the opposite.  Since
+$\ket{\Omega}$ is invariant under exchanging its two factors, $\ket{\psi}$ is
+invariant under exchanging the two players' registers, and the two players use
+identical measurements; the strategy is symmetric in the sense of the source.
+
+The flags are perfectly anticorrelated, so on each branch exactly one player
+plays the role assigned to flag~$0$.  On the branch $f_{\mathrm A} = 0$, if the
+first player receives the constraint it measures copy~$1$ while the second
+player, whose flag reads $1$, answers its variable question from copy~$1$ as
+well; if the roles are exchanged, both act on copy~$2$.  In every case the pair
+of measurements performed is the canonical perfect pair on one maximally
+entangled copy, and the branch $f_{\mathrm A} = 1$ is its mirror image.  The
+value is again $1$.  The correlation of the two players' $\Variable_1$
+observables is, branch by branch, the product of two traces of $\sigma^X \ot
+\Id$ against maximally mixed states, hence $0$ as in
+\eqref{eq:zero-correlation}, and the cross terms between the two flag branches
+vanish because the observables are flag-diagonal.  So
+\eqref{eq:forced-correlation} fails for a symmetric strategy of value $1$,
+and the same computation refutes the $\Variable_5$ relations.  Again
+$\Delta_1 = \Delta_5 = 1$.%
+\footnote{This strategy is the player-role symmetrization of the previous one,
+so the symmetrization construction of \path{lem:symmetric-strat}
+(\path{references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex}, lines~94--130)
+does not repair the statement either: it is value-preserving and moves the two
+role-dependent families into two blocks of one family, which is exactly what
+the flag register does above.  The value, the swap invariance, and the two
+vanishing correlations have also been verified numerically for the explicit
+$32$-dimensional local spaces described here.}
+
+\section{What the cited self-test provides}
+
+The source imports the theorem from \cite[Theorem~6.9]{Coladangelo2017Robust},

+whose notion of robust self-testing is stated for a linear constraint system
+game in the ordinary one-way presentation: one player receives a vertex $v$,
+that is a constraint, and answers with observables $A^{(v)}_e$ for the
+variables $e$ occurring in it, while the other receives a variable $e$ and
+answers with an observable $B_e$.%
+\footnote{\path{references/cs-paper/self-testing.tex}, lines~669--689 for the
+definition and lines~706--724 for the theorem; the Magic Square instance is at
+\path{references/cs-paper/specific-games.tex}, lines~111--135.}
+The conclusion compares $\phi_{\mathrm A} A^{(v)}_e \phi_{\mathrm A}^\dagger$
+with an ideal representation $\tau(e)$ and
+$\phi_{\mathrm B} B_e \phi_{\mathrm B}^\dagger$ with its conjugate.  In that
+game the first player never receives a bare variable question, so the theorem
+constrains one player's constraint observables and the other player's variable
+observables, and nothing else.
+
+The source relabels this conclusion for the role-symmetric game, in which each
+player has both kinds of question, and asserts it for both players' variable
+observables.  The step from the cited conclusion to the printed one is exactly
+the cross-player agreement isolated in Section~\ref{sec:forces}, and the
+strategies of Sections~\ref{sec:counterexample} and~\ref{sec:symmetric} show
+that neither the value hypothesis nor symmetry supplies it.
+
+\section{The correction}
+\label{sec:repair}
+
+Recall that a measurement $\{M_a\}$ is \emph{consistent} on a state
+$\ket{\psi} \in \mH \ot \mH$ when
+$(M_a \ot \Id)\ket{\psi} = (\Id \ot M_a)\ket{\psi}$ for every outcome $a$, and
+that a strategy is consistent when all of its measurements are.%
+\footnote{\path{references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex},
+lines~144--174; \path{def:consistent-measurement} and
+\path{def:consistent-strategy} in
+\path{blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex}, formalized as
+\leanid{MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsConsistentOn} and
+\leanid{MIPStarRE.QPBT.IsConsistentStrategyOn}.}
+For a symmetric strategy and a two-outcome measurement with observable
+$\mathcal O = M_0 - M_1$, consistency gives
+\[
+  \bra{\psi}\, \mathcal O \ot \mathcal O \,\ket{\psi}
+  = \bra{\psi}\, (\mathcal O \ot \Id)(\mathcal O \ot \Id) \,\ket{\psi}
+  = \bra{\psi}\, \mathcal O^2 \ot \Id \,\ket{\psi} = 1 ,
+\]
+which is precisely the assertion \eqref{eq:forced-correlation} that the
+conclusion forces.  Consistency is thus the missing hypothesis, and it is not an
+artefact of the $\eps = 0$ analysis: it is the property that ties the untested
+same-question pair to the tested constraint--variable pairs.
+
+\paragraph{The adopted class.}
+Owner decision B5 adopts the class of symmetric consistent strategies and
+allows a further adjustment provided the corrected statement is both correct
+and sufficient for the source's application.  Two observations shape the
+adjustment.  First, the proof below uses consistency only for the two
+distinguished variable measurements and only in the cross-player form
+$(A^{\Variable_j}_b \ot \Id)\ket\psi \approx (\Id \ot B^{\Variable_j}_b)\ket\psi$;
+it never uses that $\ket\psi$ is swap-invariant or that $A = B$.  Second, the
+source's application (Section~\ref{sec:sufficiency}) does not have exact
+consistency: it derives the agreement of the two variable measurements from
+the consistency subtests of the Pauli basis test, up to an error of order
+$\eps$, and its Lean counterpart is not a symmetric strategy at all.  The
+statement is therefore taken in the robust form of item~4 of Section~2: an
+arbitrary strategy whose defects \eqref{eq:defect} at $\Variable_1$ and
+$\Variable_5$ are at most $\delta$, with $\sqrt\eps$ replaced by
+$\eta = \sqrt\eps + \sqrt\delta$ in every estimate of the conclusion.  The
+decided class is contained in it as the case $\delta = 0$: for a symmetric
+strategy, $\Delta_j = 0$ is exactly the consistency of $\{M^{\Variable_j}_b\}$
+on $\ket\psi$ (\leanid{MIPStarRE.QPBT.msVariableConsistencyDefect\_eq\_zero\_of\_isConsistent}),
+and the conclusion is then the source's display verbatim.  The two
+counterexamples have $\Delta_1 = \Delta_5 = 1$, so the hypothesis excludes
+them, and at $\eps = \delta = 0$ the hypothesis is literally the assertion
+\eqref{eq:forced-correlation} that the conclusion forces; there is no room
+left for a counterexample of the same kind.
+
+\paragraph{Derivation from the cited self-test.}
+Let $\strategy = (\ket{\psi}, A, B)$ satisfy the hypotheses.  Conditioning on
+the orientation in which the first player receives the constraint gives a
+strategy for the one-way linear constraint system game of value at least
+$1-2\eps$, and exactly $1-\eps$ if $\strategy$ is symmetric.  After a Naimark
+dilation of both players' measurements, which does not change any Born
+probability, \cite[Theorem~6.9]{Coladangelo2017Robust} applies to this
+one-way strategy and yields $\phi_{\mathrm A}, \phi_{\mathrm B}, \ket\aux$ with
+(\path{thm:ms-rigidity},~1) at scale $\sqrt\eps$ and with the relations for
+the second player's variable observables, $\Id \ot \tilde B^{\Variable_1}_b
+\approx_{\sqrt\eps} \Id \ot (\sigma^X_b)_{\mathrm B'}$ and likewise for
+$\Variable_5$, after the local change of basis noted in the source.  (The
+robust theorem is stated for projective measurements; the passage from the
+dilated projections back to the original effects costs the leakage of the
+dilated operators out of the range of the dilation, which is bounded by the
+cell-consistency masses of a strategy of value $1-\eps$, as in the transfer
+layer of the formalization.)  For the first player, the hypothesis gives
+\[
+  (\tilde A^{\Variable_j}_b \ot \Id)\,\phi\ket\psi
+  = \phi\,(A^{\Variable_j}_b \ot \Id)\ket\psi
+  \approx_{\sqrt\delta}
+  \phi\,(\Id \ot B^{\Variable_j}_b)\ket\psi
+  = (\Id \ot \tilde B^{\Variable_j}_b)\,\phi\ket\psi,
+\]
+where $\phi = \phi_{\mathrm A} \ot \phi_{\mathrm B}$ and $\approx_{\sqrt\delta}$
+is closeness in norm; the second player's relation and
+(\path{thm:ms-rigidity},~1) move the right-hand side to
+$(\Id \ot \sigma^W_b)\ket\Theta$, and
+$(\Id \ot \sigma^W_b)\ket{\EPR_2}^{\ot 2} = (\sigma^W_b \ot \Id)\ket{\EPR_2}^{\ot 2}$
+because $\sigma^X_b$ and $\sigma^Z_b$ are real symmetric.  Every operator
+involved is a contraction, so the first player's relations hold in norm at
+scale $\sqrt\eps + \sqrt\delta$, hence as $\approx_\eta$ estimates of the
+squared distance.  The anticommutation consequences follow from the four
+relations as in the source: $(\tilde A^{\Variable_1}\tilde A^{\Variable_5}
+\ot \Id)\ket\Theta$ is within $O(\eta)$ of
+$(\sigma^X\sigma^Z \ot \Id)\ket\Theta$ by replacing the two factors one at a
+time, the second replacement using the same transposition identity to move
+$\sigma^Z$ to the other side where it commutes with $\tilde A^{\Variable_1}$;
+the reversed product is within $O(\eta)$ of
+$(\sigma^Z\sigma^X \ot \Id)\ket\Theta = -(\sigma^X\sigma^Z \ot \Id)\ket\Theta$.
+Bounds of order $\eta$ in norm are bounds of order $\eta^2 \le 2(\eps+\delta)
+\le 2\eta$ in the squared distance for $\eta \le 1$, and for $\eta > 1$ every
+estimate is trivial, so one universal constant serves all parameters.
+
+\paragraph{The formal route.}
+The formalization does not import the cited theorem.  Its rigidity chain
+(\ghissue{101}--\ghissue{104}) works on the projective dilation of an
+arbitrary strategy and derives, from the value alone, the approximate
+anticommutation of each player's own $\Variable_1$ and $\Variable_5$
+reflections on the dilated state
+(\leanid{MIPStarRE.QPBT.MagicSquareRigidity.msVarObsA\_anticommute} and its
+counterpart for the second player), together with exact swap isometries built
+from those reflections and transfer theorems that pull every post-isometry
+estimate back from the dilation to the original strategy at the cost of the
+cell-consistency masses.  What the value cannot give is that the two players'
+reflections agree on the dilated state, which the joint extraction of
+$\ket{\EPR_2}^{\ot 2} \ot \ket\aux$ needs.  This is exactly what the hypothesis
+supplies: the defect \eqref{eq:defect} of the original measurements transfers
+to the dilated reflections through the same leakage bounds,
+\[
+  \bigl\| \bigl( X_{\mathrm A} \ot \Id - \Id \ot X_{\mathrm B} \bigr)
+    \ket{\psi'} \bigr\|^2 \le 864\,\eps + 6\,\delta
+\]
+for the dilated $\Variable_j$ reflections $X_{\mathrm A}, X_{\mathrm B}$ on the
+dilated state $\ket{\psi'}$
+(\leanid{MIPStarRE.QPBT.MagicSquareRigidity.msVarObsA\_close\_msVarObsB}).  In
+this route the hypothesis enters through the state estimate
+(\path{thm:ms-rigidity},~1), and all operator relations then follow for both
+players alike; this is why the corrected statement carries $\eta$ uniformly.
+The remaining work, owned by \ghissue{105}, is listed in
+Section~\ref{sec:formal}.
+
+\section{Sufficiency for the source's application}
+\label{sec:sufficiency}
+
+The only use of the theorem is in the analysis of the Pauli basis test.%
+\footnote{\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex},
+lines~152--155 for the symmetric strategy $\strategy = (\ket\psi, M)$ of the
+test, lines~197--266 for Lemma~\path{lem:qld-win-implications}, and
+lines~326--350 for the invocation.}
+There, for each anticommuting tuple $\omega$, the measurements of the test
+strategy for the Magic Square questions labelled by $\omega$ form a strategy
+$\strategy_\omega = (\ket\psi, M^{\cdot,\omega})$ for $\game^{\MS}$ of value
+$\Lambda_\omega = 1 - \eps_\omega$ with $\E_\omega \eps_\omega = O(\eps)$
+(item~6 of the lemma), and the theorem is invoked for each $\omega$ to obtain
+$\Id \ot M^{\Variable_1,\omega} M^{\Variable_5,\omega}
+\approx_{\sqrt{\eps_\omega}} -\Id \ot M^{\Variable_5,\omega} M^{\Variable_1,\omega}$,
+the anticommutation consequence for the second player, which is then
+averaged over $\omega$ with Jensen's inequality.  The corrected theorem needs
+in addition the defects $\Delta_1(\strategy_\omega), \Delta_5(\strategy_\omega)$.
+They are available from the lemma: item~7 states that, on average over
+anticommuting $\omega$, the first player's trace-postprocessed point
+measurement $\{P_a\}$ agrees with the second player's $\Variable_1$ measurement,
+$P_a \ot \Id \simeq_\eps \Id \ot M^{\Variable_1,\omega}_a$, and the lemma's
+final clause gives the same with the tensor factors interchanged; item~1
+states that the point measurements are consistent between the players,
+$P_a \ot \Id \simeq_\eps \Id \ot P_a$.  Two applications of the triangle
+inequality, after converting $\simeq_\eps$ to $\approx_\eps$ by the lemma's own
+final clause, give
+$M^{\Variable_1,\omega}_a \ot \Id \approx_\eps \Id \ot M^{\Variable_1,\omega}_a$
+on average over $\omega$, that is, $\E_\omega \Delta_1(\strategy_\omega)
+= O(\eps)$, and likewise for $\Variable_5$ with the $Z$-basis point
+measurement.  Applying the corrected theorem with $\delta_\omega =
+\Delta_1(\strategy_\omega) + \Delta_5(\strategy_\omega)$ gives the
+anticommutation with error $\sqrt{\eps_\omega} + \sqrt{\delta_\omega}$, and
+Jensen's inequality bounds its average by
+$\sqrt{\E\eps_\omega} + \sqrt{\E\delta_\omega} = O(\sqrt\eps)$, which is the
+bound the source obtains.  The application thus goes through with one extra
+triangle inequality and no new input.
+
+The Lean side of the application confirms both halves of this.  The induced
+strategy \leanid{MIPStarRE.QPBT.ProjectiveSetting.msStrategyAt} is an
+arbitrary strategy of \leanid{MIPStarRE.QPBT.msGame} with separate local
+spaces for the two players, not a symmetric strategy, which is why the
+corrected theorem is stated for arbitrary strategies; and the two consistency
+inputs above are the statements
+\leanid{MIPStarRE.QPBT.win\_ms\_cons\_approx} (item~7, both orientations, in
+the $\approx$ form) and \leanid{MIPStarRE.QPBT.pointObs\_self\_consistent}
+(item~1, in observable form) of
+\doclink{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/WinImplications.lean}, from which the
+average defect of \leanid{MIPStarRE.QPBT.ProjectiveSetting.msStrategyAt} over
+anticommuting tuples is bounded by $O(\eps)$ by the same two triangle
+inequalities.  That derivation is part of the consumer packets
+(\ghissue{115} and its successors), not of the rigidity theorem.
+
+\section{Comparison with the blueprint and formalization}
+\label{sec:formal}
+
+The blueprint \cite{MIPStarREBlueprint} states \path{thm:ms-rigidity} in the
+corrected form of item~4 of Section~2, with the hypothesis \eqref{eq:defect}
+displayed and the source's unrestricted statement, its refutation, and the
+derivation above recorded in the proof and in the remark that follows the
+theorem.  The Lean declaration \leanid{MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists\_ms\_rigidity}
+carries the same statement: it quantifies over $\eps, \delta \ge 0$ and an
+arbitrary strategy of \leanid{MIPStarRE.QPBT.msGame} of value at least
+$1-\eps$ whose defects \leanid{MIPStarRE.QPBT.msVariableConsistencyDefect} at
+the cells $0$ and $4$ (the paper's $\Variable_1$ and $\Variable_5$) are at most
+$\delta$, and concludes the seven estimates of the source at scale
+$C(\sqrt\eps + \sqrt\delta)$ for one universal constant $C$, with the witness
+and distance definitions unchanged.  The statement-level \verb|\leanok| records
+that the Lean statement matches the blueprint statement; the proof is the
+tracked \verb|sorry| owned by \ghissue{105}, and no proof-level
+\verb|\leanok| is claimed.  Three sorry-free companions accompany it:
+\leanid{MIPStarRE.QPBT.msVariableConsistencyDefect\_eq\_zero\_of\_isConsistent}
+shows that a symmetric consistent strategy has zero defects;
+\leanid{MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists\_ms\_rigidity\_of\_symmetric\_consistent}
+derives from the theorem its specialization to that class, whose conclusion is
+the source's display; and
+\leanid{MIPStarRE.QPBT.MagicSquareRigidity.msVarObsA\_close\_msVarObsB}
+transfers the hypothesis to the dilated reflections.
+
+What remains for \ghissue{105} is the assembly of the corrected theorem from
+the chain: the approximate anticommutation and cross-commutation of the second
+logical pair, the reflections at the paper's $\Variable_2$ and $\Variable_4$,
+by the same solution-group computation; the joint swap-isometry extraction of
+the two EPR pairs from each player's two anticommuting pairs and from the
+cross-player agreement above, giving (\path{thm:ms-rigidity},~1) at scale
+$\sqrt\eps + \sqrt\delta$; the intertwining of each player's extracted qubit
+observables with $\sigma^X$ and $\sigma^Z$; and the post-isometry transfers,
+which already exist.  Nothing in this list needs symmetry, and nothing needs
+consistency beyond the two defects in the hypothesis.
+
+\section{Conclusion}
+
+The verdict is a theorem-level gap: the rigidity theorem for the Magic Square
+game is false as printed.  Its conclusion forces the two players' $\Variable_1$
+and $\Variable_5$ measurements to agree on the shared state, while the
+role-symmetric game never sends the same question to both players, and a
+perfect strategy that answers the two orientations on two independent
+maximally entangled copies violates the conclusion at $\eps = 0$; so does its
+symmetric player-role symmetrization, so symmetry alone does not repair the
+statement.  The adopted correction assumes that agreement, measured by the
+defect \eqref{eq:defect} at the two distinguished variables, and replaces
+$\sqrt\eps$ by $\sqrt\eps + \sqrt\delta$; symmetric consistent strategies are
+its case $\delta = 0$, both counterexamples have defect $1$, the source's
+application supplies the defect up to $O(\eps)$ from its own consistency
+subtests, and the cited one-way self-test proves the corrected statement.
+The blueprint and \leanid{MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists\_ms\_rigidity} now carry this
+form; its proof is the assembly tracked by \ghissue{105}.
+

    60	\begin{remark}
    61	  Unless specified otherwise, all strategies considered in this paper are tensor

    68	\begin{definition}[Projective strategies]
    69	  \label{def:projective-strategy}
    70	  We say that a strategy $\strategy = (\ket{\psi}, A, B)$ is \emph{projective} if
    71	  all the measurements $\{A^x_a\}_a$ and $\{B^y_b\}_b$ are projective.
    72	\end{definition}

    74	\begin{definition}\label{rem:symmetric-games}
    75		A game $\game = (\cal{X}, \cal{Y}, \cal{A}, \cal{B}, \mu, D)$ is
    76	  \emph{symmetric} if the question and answer alphabets are the same for both
    77	  players (i.e.\
    78	  $\cal{X} = \cal{Y}$ and $\cal{A} = \cal{B}$), the distribution $\mu$ is
    79	  symmetric (i.e.\
    80	  $\mu(x,y) = \mu(y,x)$), and the decision predicate $D$ treats both players
    81	  symmetrically (i.e.\ for all $x,y,a,b$, $D(x,y,a,b) = D(y,x,b,a)$).
    82	 
    83	We call a strategy $\strategy = (\ket{\psi}, A, B)$
    84	  \emph{symmetric} if $\ket{\psi}$ is a (pure) state in $\mH \otimes \mH$, for some
    85	  Hilbert space $\mH$, that is invariant under permutation of the two factors,
    86	  and the measurement operators of both players are identical.
    87	\end{definition}
    88	
    89	We often specify symmetric games $\game$ and symmetric strategies $\strategy$ using
    90	  a compact notation: we write $\game = (\cal{X}, \cal{A}, \mu, D)$ and
    91	  $\strategy = (\ket{\psi}, M)$ where $M$ denotes the set of measurement
    92	  operators for both players.

    94	\begin{lemma}\label{lem:symmetric-strat}
    95	  Let $\game = (\cal{X}, \cal{A},  \mu, D)$ be a symmetric game
    96	  such that $\val^*(\game) = 1-\eps$ for some $\eps\geq 0$.
    97	  Then there exists a symmetric and projective strategy
    98	  $\strategy=(\ket{\psi},M)$ such that $\val^*(\game,\strategy)\geq 1-\eps$.
    99	\end{lemma}
   100	
   101	\begin{proof}
   102	  By definition for any $\eps'>\eps$ there exists a strategy $\strategy'= (\ket{\psi'},A,B)$ such
   103	  that $\val^*(\game,\strategy')\geq 1-\eps'$.
   104	Using Naimark's theorem (Theorem~\ref{thm:naimark}) we can assume
   105	without loss of generality that $\ket{\psi'}\in\C_{\alice'}^d\otimes \C_{\bob'}^d$ for some integer $d$
   106	  and that for every $x$, $A^x$ and $B^x$ are projective measurements.
   107	Let
   108	  \[
   109	    \ket{\psi} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \big( \ket{0}_\alice \ket{1}_\bob
   110	    \ket{\psi'}_{\alice'\bob'} + \ket{1}_\alice \ket{0}_\bob
   111	    \ket{\psi'_\tau}_{\alice'\bob'}\big) \in (\C_{\alice}^2 \otimes
   112	    \C_{\alice'}^d) \otimes (\C_\bob^2 \otimes \C_{\bob'}^d)\;,
   113	  \]
   114	  where $\ket{\psi'_\tau}$ is obtained from $\ket{\psi}$ by permuting the two
   115	  players' registers.
   116	  Observe that $\ket{\psi}$ is invariant under permutation of $\alice\alice'$
   117	  and $\bob\bob'$.
   118	
   119	  For any question $x\in \cal{X}$ define the measurement $M^x = \{M^x_a\}_{a \in \cal{A}}$
   120	  acting on the Hilbert space $\C^2 \otimes \C^d$ as follows:
   121	  \[
   122	  	M^x_a = \ketbra{0}{0} \otimes A^x_a + \ketbra{1}{1} \otimes B^x_a \;,
   123	  \]
   124		i.e.\ for $\ket{\varphi} \in \C^d$, $M^x_a(\ket{0}\ket{\varphi})=\ket{0}A^x_a\ket{\varphi}$ and $M^x_a(\ket{1}\ket{\varphi})=\ket{1}B^x_a\ket{\varphi}$.
   125	  When Alice receives question $x$, she measures $M^x$ on registers $\alice \alice'$, and when Bob receives 
   126	  question $y$, he measures $M^y$ on registers $\bob \bob'$.
   127	Using that by assumption the decision predicate $D$ for $\game$ is symmetric,
   128	  it is not hard to verify that $\val^*(\game,\strategy) =
   129	  \val^*(\game,\strategy')$.
   130	\end{proof}

   132	\begin{definition}
   133	  \label{def:comm-strategy}
   134	  Let $\game = (\cal{X}, \cal{Y}, \cal{A}, \cal{B}, \mu, D)$ be a game, and let
   135	  $\strategy = (\ket{\psi}, A, B)$ be a strategy for $\game$ such that  $\mH_A = \mH_B$.
   136	  Let $S \subseteq \cal{X} \times \cal{Y}$ denote the support of the question
   137	  distribution $\mu$, i.e.\ the set of $(x,y)$ such that $\mu(x,y)>0$.
   138	  We say that $\strategy$ is a \emph{commuting strategy for $\game$} if for all
   139	  question pairs $(x, y) \in S$, we have $[A^x_a, B^y_b] = 0$ 
   140	  for all $a
   141	  \in \cal{A}, b \in \cal{B}$, where $[A, B] = AB - BA$ denotes the commutator.
   142	\end{definition}

   144	\begin{definition}[Consistent measurements]
   145	  \label{def:consistent-measurement}
   146	  Let $\cal{A}$ be a finite set, let $\ket{\psi} \in \mH \otimes \mH$ be a
   147	  state, and let $\{ M_a \}_{a \in \cal{A}}$ be a projective measurement on
   148	  $\mH$.
   149	  We say that \emph{$\{M_a\}_{a \in \cal{A}}$ is consistent on $\ket{\psi}$} if
   150	  and only if
   151	  \begin{equation*}
   152	    \forall a \in \mA\;,\quad M_a \otimes \Id_\bob\, \ket{\psi}
   153	    = \Id_\alice \otimes M_a\, \ket{\psi}\;.
   154	  \end{equation*}
   155		When the state $\ket{\psi}$ is clear from context we simply say that \emph{$\{M_a\}_{a \in \cal{A}}$ is consistent}.
   156	\end{definition}
   157	
   158	The terminology ``consistent'' arises from the fact that when the measurement $\{M_a\}$ is performed on both registers of $\ket{\psi}$, the probability of obtaining twice the same outcome is 
   159	\[ \sum_a \bra{\psi} M_a \otimes M_a \ket{\psi}\,=\, \sum_a \bra{\psi} \Id_\alice \otimes (M_a)^2 \ket{\psi} \,=\, \sum_a \bra{\psi} \Id_\alice \otimes M_a \ket{\psi} \,=\,1\;,\]
   160	where the first equality is by definition of consistency, the second uses that $\{M_a\}$ is projective, and the last uses $\sum_a M_a=\Id$. 
   161	
   162	\begin{definition}[Consistent strategies]
   163	  \label{def:consistent-strategy}
   164		Let $\strategy = (\ket{\psi}, A, B)$ be a projective strategy with state
   165	  $\ket{\psi} \in \mH \otimes \mH$, for some Hilbert space~$\mH$, which is
   166	  defined on question alphabets $\cal{X}$ and~$\cal{Y}$ and answer alphabets
   167	  $\cal{A}$ and~$\cal{B}$, respectively.
   168	  We say that the strategy $\strategy$ is \emph{consistent} if for all $x \in
   169	  \cal{X}$, the measurement $\{A^x_a\}_{a \in \cal{A}}$ is consistent on
   170	  $\ket{\psi}$ and if for all $y \in \cal{Y}$, the measurement $\{B^y_b\}_{b \in
   171	    \cal{B}}$ is consistent on $\ket{\psi}$.
   172	\end{definition}

   174	We almost always restrict our attention to symmetric strategies. In this case, consistency implies that whenever both players are sent the same question, they provide the same answer.

   157	\subsection{Strategies}
   158	\label{sec:commutation}
   159	
   160	  Let $\qldparams = (q,m,d)$ be an admissible parameter tuple (Definition~\ref{def:admissible}) and let
   161	  $\strategy = (\ket{\psi},M)$ be a strategy for
   162	  $\game^\pauli_\qldparams$ that succeeds with probability at least $1 - \eps$, where $\ket{\psi}$ is a bipartite state on registers $\alice$ and $\bob$, with associated Hilbert spaces $\mH_\alice$ and $\mH_\bob$ respectively. For notational convenience we use $M$ to denote the operators for both players; it will be clear from context which player's operators we are referring to (for example, we write $M^{(\Point,W),u}_a \otimes \Id_\bob$ to indicate that $M^{(\Point,W),u}_a$ is viewed as an operator acting on register $\alice$).
   163	  
   164	  Using Naimark's
   165	  theorem (as formulated in~\cite[Theorem 5.1]{ML20}), at the cost of
   166	  extending the state $\ket{\psi}$ by adding sufficiently many qubits
   167	  initialized in the $\ket{0}$ state we may assume
   168	  that the measurements in $\strategy$ are projective. Let
   169	  \[ \ket{\psi'} = (\ket{\psi} \otimes \ket{0 \cdots 0} \otimes \ket{0
   170	      \cdots 0})_{\alice \bob} \]
   171	  be the extended state. In the remainder of this section, we
   172	  will work with the projective strategy on the extended state, which we continue labeling $\ket{\psi}$ (instead of $\ket{\psi'}$) for notational convenience.
   173	
   174	We introduce several additional notational shorthands. By definition the strategy $\strategy$ contains measurement
   175	  operators for each of the possible question types and content
   176	  summarized in \cref{fig:decider_pauli}, such as $\{M^{(\Point,
   177	    W),y}_a\}_{a\in\F_q}$ for all $y\in\F_q^m$, etc. 
   178	For ``line'' questions (of type $\ALine$ or $\DLine$) we will use
   179	 $\Line$ as a formal placeholder for either type $\ALine$ or $\DLine$;
   180	  which type is meant will be clear from the nature of the
   181	  line. Moreover, we will use $\ell$ to denote the description of
   182	  either an axis-parallel line (given by a pair $\ell=(u_0, s)$) or a
   183	  diagonal line (given by a triple $\ell=(u_0, s, v)$). We also introduce the following collection of observables constructed from the
   184	  measurement operators in the strategy. 	
   185		For every $u \in
   186	  \F_q^m$, $r \in \F_q$, and $W \in \{X, Z\}$, define
   187	  \begin{equation}
   188	    W^r(u) =\sum_{a\in\F_q} (-1)^{\tr(ar)}  M^{(\Point, W), u}_a\;. \label{eq:qld-strat-obs}
   189	  \end{equation}
   190		The observable $W^r(u)$ acts on register $\alice$ or $\bob$ depending on whether $M^{(\Point, W), u}_a$ is viewed as being an operator acting on register $\alice$ or $\bob$; this will be made clear from context.
   191		
   192	
   193	
   194	
   195	Recall the definitions of (anti-)commuting tuple given at the start of Section~\ref{sec:qld-prelim}. 
   196	
   197	\begin{lemma}
   198	\label{lem:qld-win-implications}
   199	Assume that $\strategy$ succeeds in $\game^\pauli_\qldparams$ with probability at least $1-\eps$, for some $\eps\geq 0$. Then the following hold: 
   200		\begin{enumerate}
   201			\item \label{enu:qld-cons} (\textbf{Consistency check}) On average over $(\tvar,x)$ sampled from the question distribution of $\game^\pauli_\qldparams$, we have that $M^{\tvar,x}_a \otimes \Id_\bob \simeq_\eps \Id_\alice \otimes M^{\tvar,x}_a$.
   202			\item \label{enu:qld-ld} (\textbf{Low-degree check})
   203	                  For all $W \in \{X,Z\}$, on average over $(\line,u)$
   204	                  drawn from the line-point distribution (see
   205	                  Definition~\ref{def:line-point-dist}), we
   206	                  have $M^{(\Line,W),\line}_{[\eval_u(\cdot) = a]} \otimes \Id_\bob \simeq_\eps \Id_\alice \otimes M^{(\Point,W),u}_a$, where the answer summation is over $a \in \F_q$. 
   207			
   208		\item \label{enu:qld-pauli-basis-cons} (\textbf{Pauli basis consistency check}) For all $W \in \{X,Z\}$, on average over $u \in \F_q^m$, we have $M^{(\Point,W),u}_a \otimes \Id_\bob \simeq_\eps \Id_\alice \otimes M^{(\Pauli,W)}_{[g_h(u)=a]}$ where $M^{(\Pauli,W)}_{[g_h(u)=a]} = \sum_{h \in \F_q^{\nqubits} : g_h(u) = a} M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h$ and $g_h$ is the low-degree encoding of $h$. 
   209		
   210			\item \label{enu:qld-comm} (\textbf{Commutation check}) For all $W \in \{X,Z\}$, on average over commuting $\omega = (u_\xpt,u_\zpt,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)$, we have $M^{(\Pair,W),\omega}_a \otimes \Id_\bob \simeq_\eps \Id_\alice \otimes M^{\Pair,\omega}_{[\beta_W = a]}$, where the answer summation is over $a \in \F_2$.
   211			\item \label{enu:qld-comm-cons} (\textbf{Commutation consistency check}) For all $W \in \{X,Z\}$, on average over commuting $\omega = (u_\xpt,u_\zpt,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)$, we have $M^{(\Point,W),u_W}_{[\tr(\cdot r_W) = a]} \otimes \Id_\bob \simeq_\eps \Id_\alice \otimes M^{(\Pair,W),\omega}_{a}$, where the answer summation is over $a\in \F_2$.
   212			
   213			\item\label{enu:qld-ms} (\textbf{Magic square check}) For any anticommuting $\omega = (u_\xpt,u_\zpt,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)$ let $\Lambda_\omega$ be the value of the strategy $\Big (\ket{\psi}, \{M^{\Constraint_i,\omega}_{\alpha_1,\alpha_2,\alpha_3}\} \cup \{M^{\Variable_j,\omega}_a \} \Big )$ in the game $\game^\ms$. Then 
   214			\[
   215				\E_{\omega \, : \, \tr((r_\xpt \cdot
   216	                          u_\xpt) \cdot (r_\zpt \cdot u_\zpt)) \neq 0} \Lambda_\omega = 1 - O(\eps)\;.
   217			\]
   218	
   219		\item \label{enu:qld-ms-cons} (\textbf{Magic square consistency check}) For all $W \in \{X,Z\}$, on average over anticommuting $\omega = (u_\xpt,u_\zpt,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)$,
   220		\begin{gather}
   221			M^{(\Point,X),u_\xpt}_{[\tr(\cdot r_\xpt) = a]} \otimes \Id_\bob \simeq_\eps \Id_\alice \otimes M^{\Variable_1,\omega}_{a} \;,\\
   222			M^{(\Point,Z),u_\zpt}_{[\tr(\cdot r_\zpt) = a]} \otimes \Id_\bob \simeq_\eps \Id_\alice \otimes M^{\Variable_5,\omega}_{a}\;,
   223		\end{gather}	
   224		where the answer summations are over $\F_2$.
   225		
   226		\end{enumerate}
   227		Furthermore, all of the approximations above hold with ``$\approx_\eps$'' instead of ``$\simeq_\eps$'', and they also hold with the tensor factors interchanged.
   228	\end{lemma}

   230	\begin{proof}
   231		Since the question types are sampled according to the type graph $G^\Pauli$ of
   232	  finite size in \cref{fig:type-graph-pauli} in the game
   233	  $\game^\pauli_\qldparams$, the probability of any of the subtests of
   234	  $\decider^\pauli_\qldparams$ (described in \cref{fig:decider_pauli})
   235	  being executed is at least some universal constant.
   236	  Thus the consistency conditions expressed in Items
   237	  \ref{enu:qld-cons},~\ref{enu:qld-ld},~\ref{enu:qld-pauli-basis-cons} of the
   238	  lemma follow directly from the corresponding tests in
   239	  \cref{fig:decider_pauli} (where \Cref{enu:qld-ld} follows from the
   240	  consistency test that is a subtest of $\decider^\ld_\ldparams$) and the fact
   241	  that the strategy $\strategy$ is assumed to succeed with probability at least
   242	  $1 - \eps$ in $\game^\pauli_\qldparams$.
   243					
   244	  For the remaining items, recall that by Fact~\ref{fact:omega-anticomm-prob}
   245	  the probability that a tuple $\omega=(u_\xpt,u_\zpt,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)$ sampled as
   246	  question content for a question of type $\Pair$, $(\Pair,W)$, $\Constraint_i$
   247	  or $\Variable_j$ is commuting is at least $(1 - 3md/q) \cdot (1/2)$, which is
   248	  at least $1/4$ assuming $6md \leq q$. We claim this assumption holds
   249	  without loss of generality. Indeed, observe that the function
   250	  $\delta$ in \Cref{thm:pauli-appendix} is monotonically increasing in $a$, so without loss of generality we may assume that $a
   251	  \geq 6$.  Then it follows that we may assume that $6md \leq q$
   252	  without loss of generality, since otherwise, $\delta \geq a md /q
   253	  \geq 1$ and the conclusion of the theorem holds trivially.
   254	  The same lower bound holds for the probability that $\omega$ is anticommuting.
   255	  Therefore, the consistency conditions in
   256	  Items~\ref{enu:qld-comm},~\ref{enu:qld-comm-cons} and~\ref{enu:qld-ms-cons} of
   257	  the lemma also follow directly from the corresponding tests in
   258	  \cref{fig:decider_pauli}.
   259	  Finally, \Cref{enu:qld-ms} in the lemma follows from the fact that the Magic
   260	  Square check in \cref{fig:decider_pauli} is executed with constant probability
   261	  over the choice of a pair of questions.
   262					
   263	That all of the approximations in the Lemma statement also hold with
   264	$\simeq_\eps$ replaced by $\approx_\eps$ is immediate from Fact~\ref{fact:agreement}.
   265	\end{proof}

   239	  \end{array}
   240	\]
   241	placed in the grid, whose rows and first two columns multiply to $\Id$ and
   242	whose third column multiplies to $-\Id$.  All nine are real and symmetric.  Let
   243	$\ket{\Omega} \in \mathcal K \ot \mathcal K$ be the maximally entangled state,
   244	which is $\ket{\EPR_2}^{\ot 2}$ after reordering the qubits, and let $M$ be the
   245	measurement family that answers $\Constraint_i$ by jointly measuring the three
   246	commuting observables of row or column $i$ and answers $\Variable_j$ by the
   247	two-outcome measurement $\{(\Id \pm O_j)/2\}$.  Then $(\ket{\Omega}, M)$ is a
   248	symmetric, projective, consistent strategy of value $1$.
   249	
   250	Now give each player a copy of $\mathcal K \ot \mathcal K$ and split the two
   251	roles across the two copies: on a constraint question the first player measures
   252	copy~$1$ and the second measures copy~$2$, and on a variable question the first
   253	player measures copy~$2$ and the second measures copy~$1$.  With the state
   254	$\ket{\Omega}_{\mathrm A_1 \mathrm B_1} \ot
   255	\ket{\Omega}_{\mathrm A_2 \mathrm B_2}$, every sampled question pair consists of
   256	one constraint and one variable, so the two measurements actually performed are
   257	the canonical perfect pair acting on a single maximally entangled copy: on
   258	copy~$1$ when the first player holds the constraint, and on copy~$2$ when the
   259	second player does.  The value is therefore $1$.  The two players' $\Variable_1$
   260	observables, however, act on $\mathrm A_2$ and $\mathrm B_1$, whose joint
   261	reduced state is a product of maximally mixed states, so
   262	\begin{equation}
   263	  \bra{\psi}\,\mathcal O_A \ot \mathcal O_B\,\ket{\psi}
   264	  = \frac{\tr(\sigma^X \ot \Id)}{4} \cdot \frac{\tr(\sigma^X \ot \Id)}{4}
   265	  = 0 ,
   266	  \label{eq:zero-correlation}
   267	\end{equation}
   268	contradicting \eqref{eq:forced-correlation}.  The same computation with
   269	$\sigma^Z$ refutes the $\Variable_5$ relations.  The source statement is thus
   270	false at $\eps = 0$, and no choice of isometries or auxiliary state can repair
   271	it, since \eqref{eq:forced-correlation} used only that $\phi_{\mathrm A}$ and
   272	$\phi_{\mathrm B}$ are isometries.  In the terms of \eqref{eq:defect}, this
   273	strategy has $\Delta_1 = \Delta_5 = 1$: for $\pm1$ observables
   274	$\sum_b \|(A_b \ot \Id - \Id \ot B_b)\ket\psi\|^2
   275	= 1 - \bra\psi \mathcal O_A \ot \mathcal O_B \ket\psi$
   276	whenever the two measurements are projective on the state.
   277	
   278	\section{Symmetry does not repair the statement}
   279	\label{sec:symmetric}
   280	
   281	The strategy just described is not symmetric: the two players use different
   282	measurement families.  It is natural to hope that the source's standing
   283	restriction to symmetric strategies excludes it.  It does not.
   284	
   285	Give each player a flag qubit and two copies of $\mathcal K$, so that the local
   286	space is $\C^2 \ot \mathcal K \ot \mathcal K$, and take the state
   287	\[
   288	  \ket{\psi} = \frac{1}{\sqrt2}
   289	    \bigl( \ket{0}_{f_{\mathrm A}}\ket{1}_{f_{\mathrm B}}
   290	         + \ket{1}_{f_{\mathrm A}}\ket{0}_{f_{\mathrm B}} \bigr)
   291	    \ot \ket{\Omega}_{\mathrm A_1 \mathrm B_1}
   292	    \ot \ket{\Omega}_{\mathrm A_2 \mathrm B_2} .
   293	\]
   294	Both players use the single family
   295	\begin{align*}
   296	  M^{\Constraint_i}_a
   297	    &= \ket{0}\!\bra{0}_f \ot (M^{\Constraint_i}_a)_1 \ot \Id_2
   298	     + \ket{1}\!\bra{1}_f \ot \Id_1 \ot (M^{\Constraint_i}_a)_2 , \\
   299	  M^{\Variable_j}_b
   300	    &= \ket{0}\!\bra{0}_f \ot \Id_1 \ot (M^{\Variable_j}_b)_2
   301	     + \ket{1}\!\bra{1}_f \ot (M^{\Variable_j}_b)_1 \ot \Id_2 :
   302	\end{align*}
   303	a player whose flag reads $0$ answers constraints from copy~$1$ and variables
   304	from copy~$2$, and a player whose flag reads $1$ does the opposite.  Since
   305	$\ket{\Omega}$ is invariant under exchanging its two factors, $\ket{\psi}$ is
   306	invariant under exchanging the two players' registers, and the two players use
   307	identical measurements; the strategy is symmetric in the sense of the source.
   308	
   309	The flags are perfectly anticorrelated, so on each branch exactly one player
   310	plays the role assigned to flag~$0$.  On the branch $f_{\mathrm A} = 0$, if the
   311	first player receives the constraint it measures copy~$1$ while the second
   312	player, whose flag reads $1$, answers its variable question from copy~$1$ as
   313	well; if the roles are exchanged, both act on copy~$2$.  In every case the pair
   314	of measurements performed is the canonical perfect pair on one maximally
   315	entangled copy, and the branch $f_{\mathrm A} = 1$ is its mirror image.  The
   316	value is again $1$.  The correlation of the two players' $\Variable_1$
   317	observables is, branch by branch, the product of two traces of $\sigma^X \ot
   318	\Id$ against maximally mixed states, hence $0$ as in
   319	\eqref{eq:zero-correlation}, and the cross terms between the two flag branches
   320	vanish because the observables are flag-diagonal.  So
   321	\eqref{eq:forced-correlation} fails for a symmetric strategy of value $1$,
   322	and the same computation refutes the $\Variable_5$ relations.  Again
   323	$\Delta_1 = \Delta_5 = 1$.%
   324	\footnote{This strategy is the player-role symmetrization of the previous one,
   325	so the symmetrization construction of \path{lem:symmetric-strat}
   326	(\path{references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex}, lines~94--130)
   327	does not repair the statement either: it is value-preserving and moves the two
   328	role-dependent families into two blocks of one family, which is exactly what
   329	the flag register does above.  The value, the swap invariance, and the two
   330	vanishing correlations have also been verified numerically for the explicit

481	\label{sec:sufficiency}
   482	
   483	The only use of the theorem is in the analysis of the Pauli basis test.%
   484	\footnote{\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex},
   485	lines~152--155 for the symmetric strategy $\strategy = (\ket\psi, M)$ of the
   486	test, lines~197--266 for Lemma~\path{lem:qld-win-implications}, and
   487	lines~326--350 for the invocation.}
   488	There, for each anticommuting tuple $\omega$, the measurements of the test
   489	strategy for the Magic Square questions labelled by $\omega$ form a strategy
   490	$\strategy_\omega = (\ket\psi, M^{\cdot,\omega})$ for $\game^{\MS}$ of value
   491	$\Lambda_\omega = 1 - \eps_\omega$ with $\E_\omega \eps_\omega = O(\eps)$
   492	(item~6 of the lemma), and the theorem is invoked for each $\omega$ to obtain
   493	$\Id \ot M^{\Variable_1,\omega} M^{\Variable_5,\omega}
   494	\approx_{\sqrt{\eps_\omega}} -\Id \ot M^{\Variable_5,\omega} M^{\Variable_1,\omega}$,
   495	the anticommutation consequence for the second player, which is then
   496	averaged over $\omega$ with Jensen's inequality.  The corrected theorem needs
   497	in addition the defects $\Delta_1(\strategy_\omega), \Delta_5(\strategy_\omega)$.
   498	They are available from the lemma: item~7 states that, on average over
   499	anticommuting $\omega$, the first player's trace-postprocessed point
   500	measurement $\{P_a\}$ agrees with the second player's $\Variable_1$ measurement,
   501	$P_a \ot \Id \simeq_\eps \Id \ot M^{\Variable_1,\omega}_a$, and the lemma's
   502	final clause gives the same with the tensor factors interchanged; item~1
   503	states that the point measurements are consistent between the players,
   504	$P_a \ot \Id \simeq_\eps \Id \ot P_a$.  Two applications of the triangle
   505	inequality, after converting $\simeq_\eps$ to $\approx_\eps$ by the lemma's own
   506	final clause, give
   507	$M^{\Variable_1,\omega}_a \ot \Id \approx_\eps \Id \ot M^{\Variable_1,\omega}_a$
   508	on average over $\omega$, that is, $\E_\omega \Delta_1(\strategy_\omega)
   509	= O(\eps)$, and likewise for $\Variable_5$ with the $Z$-basis point
   510	measurement.  Applying the corrected theorem with $\delta_\omega =
   511	\Delta_1(\strategy_\omega) + \Delta_5(\strategy_\omega)$ gives the
   512	anticommutation with error $\sqrt{\eps_\omega} + \sqrt{\delta_\omega}$, and
   513	Jensen's inequality bounds its average by
   514	$\sqrt{\E\eps_\omega} + \sqrt{\E\delta_\omega} = O(\sqrt\eps)$, which is the
   515	bound the source obtains.  The application thus goes through with one extra
   516	triangle inequality and no new input.
   517	
   518	The Lean side of the application confirms both halves of this.  The induced
   519	strategy \leanid{MIPStarRE.QPBT.ProjectiveSetting.msStrategyAt} is an
   520	arbitrary strategy of \leanid{MIPStarRE.QPBT.msGame} with separate local
   521	spaces for the two players, not a symmetric strategy, which is why the
   522	corrected theorem is stated for arbitrary strategies; and the two consistency
   523	inputs above are the statements
   524	\leanid{MIPStarRE.QPBT.win\_ms\_cons\_approx} (item~7, both orientations, in
   525	the $\approx$ form) and \leanid{MIPStarRE.QPBT.pointObs\_self\_consistent}
   526	(item~1, in observable form) of
   527	\doclink{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/WinImplications.lean}, from which the
   528	average defect of \leanid{MIPStarRE.QPBT.ProjectiveSetting.msStrategyAt} over
   529	anticommuting tuples is bounded by $O(\eps)$ by the same two triangle
   530	inequalities.  That derivation is part of the consumer packets
   531	(\ghissue{115} and its successors), not of the rigidity theorem.
   532	
   533	\section{Comparison with the blueprint and formalization}
   534	\label{sec:formal}
   535	
   536	The blueprint \cite{MIPStarREBlueprint} states \path{thm:ms-rigidity} in the
   537	corrected form of item~4 of Section~2, with the hypothesis \eqref{eq:defect}
   538	displayed and the source's unrestricted statement, its refutation, and the
   539	derivation above recorded in the proof and in the remark that follows the
   540	theorem.  The Lean declaration \leanid{MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists\_ms\_rigidity}
   541	carries the same statement: it quantifies over $\eps, \delta \ge 0$ and an
   542	arbitrary strategy of \leanid{MIPStarRE.QPBT.msGame} of value at least
   543	$1-\eps$ whose defects \leanid{MIPStarRE.QPBT.msVariableConsistencyDefect} at
   544	the cells $0$ and $4$ (the paper's $\Variable_1$ and $\Variable_5$) are at most
   545	$\delta$, and concludes the seven estimates of the source at scale
   546	$C(\sqrt\eps + \sqrt\delta)$ for one universal constant $C$, with the witness
   547	and distance definitions unchanged.  The statement-level \verb|\leanok| records
   548	that the Lean statement matches the blueprint statement; the proof is the
   549	tracked \verb|sorry| owned by \ghissue{105}, and no proof-level
   550	\verb|\leanok| is claimed.  Three sorry-free companions accompany it:
   551	\leanid{MIPStarRE.QPBT.msVariableConsistencyDefect\_eq\_zero\_of\_isConsistent}
   552	shows that a symmetric consistent strategy has zero defects;
   553	\leanid{MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists\_ms\_rigidity\_of\_symmetric\_consistent}
   554	derives from the theorem its specialization to that class, whose conclusion is
   555	the source's display; and
   556	\leanid{MIPStarRE.QPBT.MagicSquareRigidity.msVarObsA\_close\_msVarObsB}
   557	transfers the hypothesis to the dilated reflections.
   558	
   559	What remains for \ghissue{105} is the assembly of the corrected theorem from
   560	the chain: the approximate anticommutation and cross-commutation of the second
   561	logical pair, the reflections at the paper's $\Variable_2$ and $\Variable_4$,
   562	by the same solution-group computation; the joint swap-isometry extraction of
   563	the two EPR pairs from each player's two anticommuting pairs and from the
   564	cross-player agreement above, giving (\path{thm:ms-rigidity},~1) at scale
   565	$\sqrt\eps + \sqrt\delta$; the intertwining of each player's extracted qubit
   566	observables with $\sigma^X$ and $\sigma^Z$; and the post-isometry transfers,
   567	which already exist.  Nothing in this list needs symmetry, and nothing needs
   568	consistency beyond the two defects in the hypothesis.
   569	
   570	\section{Conclusion}
   571	
   572	The verdict is a theorem-level gap: the rigidity theorem for the Magic Square
   573	game is false as printed.  Its conclusion forces the two players' $\Variable_1$
   574	and $\Variable_5$ measurements to agree on the shared state, while the
   575	role-symmetric game never sends the same question to both players, and a
   576	perfect strategy that answers the two orientations on two independent
   577	maximally entangled copies violates the conclusion at $\eps = 0$; so does its
   578	symmetric player-role symmetrization, so symmetry alone does not repair the
   579	statement.  The adopted correction assumes that agreement, measured by the
   580	defect \eqref{eq:defect} at the two distinguished variables, and replaces
   581	$\sqrt\eps$ by $\sqrt\eps + \sqrt\delta$; symmetric consistent strategies are
   582	its case $\delta = 0$, both counterexamples have defect $1$, the source's
   583	application supplies the defect up to $O(\eps)$ from its own consistency
   584	subtests, and the cited one-way self-test proves the corrected statement.
   585	The blueprint and \leanid{MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists\_ms\_rigidity} now carry this
   586	form; its proof is the assembly tracked by \ghissue{105}.

   333	\section{What the cited self-test provides}
   334	
   335	The source imports the theorem from \cite[Theorem~6.9]{Coladangelo2017Robust},
   336	whose notion of robust self-testing is stated for a linear constraint system
   337	game in the ordinary one-way presentation: one player receives a vertex $v$,
   338	that is a constraint, and answers with observables $A^{(v)}_e$ for the
   339	variables $e$ occurring in it, while the other receives a variable $e$ and
   340	answers with an observable $B_e$.%
   341	\footnote{\path{references/cs-paper/self-testing.tex}, lines~669--689 for the
   342	definition and lines~706--724 for the theorem; the Magic Square instance is at
   343	\path{references/cs-paper/specific-games.tex}, lines~111--135.}
   344	The conclusion compares $\phi_{\mathrm A} A^{(v)}_e \phi_{\mathrm A}^\dagger$
   345	with an ideal representation $\tau(e)$ and
   346	$\phi_{\mathrm B} B_e \phi_{\mathrm B}^\dagger$ with its conjugate.  In that
   347	game the first player never receives a bare variable question, so the theorem
   348	constrains one player's constraint observables and the other player's variable
   349	observables, and nothing else.
   350	
   351	The source relabels this conclusion for the role-symmetric game, in which each
   352	player has both kinds of question, and asserts it for both players' variable
   353	observables.  The step from the cited conclusion to the printed one is exactly
   354	the cross-player agreement isolated in Section~\ref{sec:forces}, and the
   355	strategies of Sections~\ref{sec:counterexample} and~\ref{sec:symmetric} show
   356	that neither the value hypothesis nor symmetry supplies it.
   357	
   358	\section{The correction}
   359	\label{sec:repair}
   360	
   361	Recall that a measurement $\{M_a\}$ is \emph{consistent} on a state
   362	$\ket{\psi} \in \mH \ot \mH$ when
   363	$(M_a \ot \Id)\ket{\psi} = (\Id \ot M_a)\ket{\psi}$ for every outcome $a$, and
   364	that a strategy is consistent when all of its measurements are.%
   365	\footnote{\path{references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex},
   366	lines~144--174; \path{def:consistent-measurement} and
   367	\path{def:consistent-strategy} in
   368	\path{blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex}, formalized as
   369	\leanid{MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsConsistentOn} and
   370	\leanid{MIPStarRE.QPBT.IsConsistentStrategyOn}.}
   371	For a symmetric strategy and a two-outcome measurement with observable
   372	$\mathcal O = M_0 - M_1$, consistency gives
   373	\[
   374	  \bra{\psi}\, \mathcal O \ot \mathcal O \,\ket{\psi}
   375	  = \bra{\psi}\, (\mathcal O \ot \Id)(\mathcal O \ot \Id) \,\ket{\psi}
   376	  = \bra{\psi}\, \mathcal O^2 \ot \Id \,\ket{\psi} = 1 ,
   377	\]
   378	which is precisely the assertion \eqref{eq:forced-correlation} that the
   379	conclusion forces.  Consistency is thus the missing hypothesis, and it is not an
   380	artefact of the $\eps = 0$ analysis: it is the property that ties the untested
   381	same-question pair to the tested constraint--variable pairs.
   382	
   383	\paragraph{The adopted class.}
   384	Owner decision B5 adopts the class of symmetric consistent strategies and
   385	allows a further adjustment provided the corrected statement is both correct
   386	and sufficient for the source's application.  Two observations shape the
   387	adjustment.  First, the proof below uses consistency only for the two
   388	distinguished variable measurements and only in the cross-player form
   389	$(A^{\Variable_j}_b \ot \Id)\ket\psi \approx (\Id \ot B^{\Variable_j}_b)\ket\psi$;
   390	it never uses that $\ket\psi$ is swap-invariant or that $A = B$.  Second, the
   391	source's application (Section~\ref{sec:sufficiency}) does not have exact
   392	consistency: it derives the agreement of the two variable measurements from
   393	the consistency subtests of the Pauli basis test, up to an error of order
   394	$\eps$, and its Lean counterpart is not a symmetric strategy at all.  The
   395	statement is therefore taken in the robust form of item~4 of Section~2: an
   396	arbitrary strategy whose defects \eqref{eq:defect} at $\Variable_1$ and
   397	$\Variable_5$ are at most $\delta$, with $\sqrt\eps$ replaced by
   398	$\eta = \sqrt\eps + \sqrt\delta$ in every estimate of the conclusion.  The
   399	decided class is contained in it as the case $\delta = 0$: for a symmetric
   400	strategy, $\Delta_j = 0$ is exactly the consistency of $\{M^{\Variable_j}_b\}$
   401	on $\ket\psi$ (\leanid{MIPStarRE.QPBT.msVariableConsistencyDefect\_eq\_zero\_of\_isConsistent}),
   402	and the conclusion is then the source's display verbatim.  The two
   403	counterexamples have $\Delta_1 = \Delta_5 = 1$, so the hypothesis excludes
   404	them, and at $\eps = \delta = 0$ the hypothesis is literally the assertion
   405	\eqref{eq:forced-correlation} that the conclusion forces; there is no room
   406	left for a counterexample of the same kind.
   407	
   408	\paragraph{Derivation from the cited self-test.}
   409	Let $\strategy = (\ket{\psi}, A, B)$ satisfy the hypotheses.  Conditioning on
   410	the orientation in which the first player receives the constraint gives a
   411	strategy for the one-way linear constraint system game of value at least
   412	$1-2\eps$, and exactly $1-\eps$ if $\strategy$ is symmetric.  After a Naimark
   413	dilation of both players' measurements, which does not change any Born
   414	probability, \cite[Theorem~6.9]{Coladangelo2017Robust} applies to this
   415	one-way strategy and yields $\phi_{\mathrm A}, \phi_{\mathrm B}, \ket\aux$ with
   416	(\path{thm:ms-rigidity},~1) at scale $\sqrt\eps$ and with the relations for
   417	the second player's variable observables, $\Id \ot \tilde B^{\Variable_1}_b
   418	\approx_{\sqrt\eps} \Id \ot (\sigma^X_b)_{\mathrm B'}$ and likewise for
   419	$\Variable_5$, after the local change of basis noted in the source.  (The
   420	robust theorem is stated for projective measurements; the passage from the
   421	dilated projections back to the original effects costs the leakage of the
   422	dilated operators out of the range of the dilation, which is bounded by the
   423	cell-consistency masses of a strategy of value $1-\eps$, as in the transfer
   424	layer of the formalization.)  For the first player, the hypothesis gives
   425	\[
   426	  (\tilde A^{\Variable_j}_b \ot \Id)\,\phi\ket\psi
   427	  = \phi\,(A^{\Variable_j}_b \ot \Id)\ket\psi
   428	  \approx_{\sqrt\delta}
   429	  \phi\,(\Id \ot B^{\Variable_j}_b)\ket\psi
   430	  = (\Id \ot \tilde B^{\Variable_j}_b)\,\phi\ket\psi,
   431	\]
   432	where $\phi = \phi_{\mathrm A} \ot \phi_{\mathrm B}$ and $\approx_{\sqrt\delta}$
   433	is closeness in norm; the second player's relation and
   434	(\path{thm:ms-rigidity},~1) move the right-hand side to
   435	$(\Id \ot \sigma^W_b)\ket\Theta$, and
   436	$(\Id \ot \sigma^W_b)\ket{\EPR_2}^{\ot 2} = (\sigma^W_b \ot \Id)\ket{\EPR_2}^{\ot 2}$
   437	because $\sigma^X_b$ and $\sigma^Z_b$ are real symmetric.  Every operator
   438	involved is a contraction, so the first player's relations hold in norm at
   439	scale $\sqrt\eps + \sqrt\delta$, hence as $\approx_\eta$ estimates of the
   440	squared distance.  The anticommutation consequences follow from the four
   441	relations as in the source: $(\tilde A^{\Variable_1}\tilde A^{\Variable_5}
   442	\ot \Id)\ket\Theta$ is within $O(\eta)$ of
   443	$(\sigma^X\sigma^Z \ot \Id)\ket\Theta$ by replacing the two factors one at a
   444	time, the second replacement using the same transposition identity to move
   445	$\sigma^Z$ to the other side where it commutes with $\tilde A^{\Variable_1}$;
   446	the reversed product is within $O(\eta)$ of
   447	$(\sigma^Z\sigma^X \ot \Id)\ket\Theta = -(\sigma^X\sigma^Z \ot \Id)\ket\Theta$.
   448	Bounds of order $\eta$ in norm are bounds of order $\eta^2 \le 2(\eps+\delta)
   449	\le 2\eta$ in the squared distance for $\eta \le 1$, and for $\eta > 1$ every
   450	estimate is trivial, so one universal constant serves all parameters.
   451	
   452	\paragraph{The formal route.}
   453	The formalization does not import the cited theorem.  Its rigidity chain
   454	(\ghissue{101}--\ghissue{104}) works on the projective dilation of an
   455	arbitrary strategy and derives, from the value alone, the approximate
   456	anticommutation of each player's own $\Variable_1$ and $\Variable_5$
   457	reflections on the dilated state
   458	(\leanid{MIPStarRE.QPBT.MagicSquareRigidity.msVarObsA\_anticommute} and its
   459	counterpart for the second player), together with exact swap isometries built
   460	from those reflections and transfer theorems that pull every post-isometry
   461	estimate back from the dilation to the original strategy at the cost of the
   462	cell-consistency masses.  What the value cannot give is that the two players'
   463	reflections agree on the dilated state, which the joint extraction of
   464	$\ket{\EPR_2}^{\ot 2} \ot \ket\aux$ needs.  This is exactly what the hypothesis
   465	supplies: the defect \eqref{eq:defect} of the original measurements transfers
   466	to the dilated reflections through the same leakage bounds,
   467	\[
   468	  \bigl\| \bigl( X_{\mathrm A} \ot \Id - \Id \ot X_{\mathrm B} \bigr)
   469	    \ket{\psi'} \bigr\|^2 \le 864\,\eps + 6\,\delta
   470	\]
   471	for the dilated $\Variable_j$ reflections $X_{\mathrm A}, X_{\mathrm B}$ on the
   472	dilated state $\ket{\psi'}$
   473	(\leanid{MIPStarRE.QPBT.MagicSquareRigidity.msVarObsA\_close\_msVarObsB}).  In
   474	this route the hypothesis enters through the state estimate
   475	(\path{thm:ms-rigidity},~1), and all operator relations then follow for both
   476	players alike; this is why the corrected statement carries $\eta$ uniformly.
   477	The remaining work, owned by \ghissue{105}, is listed in
   478	Section~\ref{sec:formal}.

   430	  = (\Id \ot \tilde B^{\Variable_j}_b)\,\phi\ket\psi,
   431	\]
   432	where $\phi = \phi_{\mathrm A} \ot \phi_{\mathrm B}$ and $\approx_{\sqrt\delta}$
   433	is closeness in norm; the second player's relation and
   434	(\path{thm:ms-rigidity},~1) move the right-hand side to
   435	$(\Id \ot \sigma^W_b)\ket\Theta$, and
   436	$(\Id \ot \sigma^W_b)\ket{\EPR_2}^{\ot 2} = (\sigma^W_b \ot \Id)\ket{\EPR_2}^{\ot 2}$
   437	because $\sigma^X_b$ and $\sigma^Z_b$ are real symmetric.  Every operator
   438	involved is a contraction, so the first player's relations hold in norm at
   439	scale $\sqrt\eps + \sqrt\delta$, hence as $\approx_\eta$ estimates of the
   440	squared distance.  The anticommutation consequences follow from the four
   441	relations as in the source: $(\tilde A^{\Variable_1}\tilde A^{\Variable_5}
   442	\ot \Id)\ket\Theta$ is within $O(\eta)$ of
   443	$(\sigma^X\sigma^Z \ot \Id)\ket\Theta$ by replacing the two factors one at a
   444	time, the second replacement using the same transposition identity to move
   445	$\sigma^Z$ to the other side where it commutes with $\tilde A^{\Variable_1}$;
   446	the reversed product is within $O(\eta)$ of
   447	$(\sigma^Z\sigma^X \ot \Id)\ket\Theta = -(\sigma^X\sigma^Z \ot \Id)\ket\Theta$.
   448	Bounds of order $\eta$ in norm are bounds of order $\eta^2 \le 2(\eps+\delta)
   449	\le 2\eta$ in the squared distance for $\eta \le 1$, and for $\eta > 1$ every
   450	estimate is trivial, so one universal constant serves all parameters.
   451	
   452	\paragraph{The formal route.}
   453	The formalization does not import the cited theorem.  Its rigidity chain
   454	(\ghissue{101}--\ghissue{104}) works on the projective dilation of an
   455	arbitrary strategy and derives, from the value alone, the approximate
   456	anticommutation of each player's own $\Variable_1$ and $\Variable_5$
   457	reflections on the dilated state
   458	(\leanid{MIPStarRE.QPBT.MagicSquareRigidity.msVarObsA\_anticommute} and its
   459	counterpart for the second player), together with exact swap isometries built
   460	from those reflections and transfer theorems that pull every post-isometry
   461	estimate back from the dilation to the original strategy at the cost of the
   462	cell-consistency masses.  What the value cannot give is that the two players'
   463	reflections agree on the dilated state, which the joint extraction of
   464	$\ket{\EPR_2}^{\ot 2} \ot \ket\aux$ needs.  This is exactly what the hypothesis
   465	supplies: the defect \eqref{eq:defect} of the original measurements transfers
   466	to the dilated reflections through the same leakage bounds,
   467	\[
   468	  \bigl\| \bigl( X_{\mathrm A} \ot \Id - \Id \ot X_{\mathrm B} \bigr)
   469	    \ket{\psi'} \bigr\|^2 \le 864\,\eps + 6\,\delta
   470	\]
   471	for the dilated $\Variable_j$ reflections $X_{\mathrm A}, X_{\mathrm B}$ on the
   472	dilated state $\ket{\psi'}$
   473	(\leanid{MIPStarRE.QPBT.MagicSquareRigidity.msVarObsA\_close\_msVarObsB}).  In
   474	this route the hypothesis enters through the state estimate
   475	(\path{thm:ms-rigidity},~1), and all operator relations then follow for both
   476	players alike; this is why the corrected statement carries $\eta$ uniformly.
   477	The remaining work, owned by \ghissue{105}, is listed in
   478	Section~\ref{sec:formal}.
   479	
   480	\section{Sufficiency for the source's application}
   481	\label{sec:sufficiency}
   482	
   483	The only use of the theorem is in the analysis of the Pauli basis test.%
   484	\footnote{\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex},
   485	lines~152--155 for the symmetric strategy $\strategy = (\ket\psi, M)$ of the
   486	test, lines~197--266 for Lemma~\path{lem:qld-win-implications}, and
   487	lines~326--350 for the invocation.}
   488	There, for each anticommuting tuple $\omega$, the measurements of the test
   489	strategy for the Magic Square questions labelled by $\omega$ form a strategy
   490	$\strategy_\omega = (\ket\psi, M^{\cdot,\omega})$ for $\game^{\MS}$ of value
   491	$\Lambda_\omega = 1 - \eps_\omega$ with $\E_\omega \eps_\omega = O(\eps)$
   492	(item~6 of the lemma), and the theorem is invoked for each $\omega$ to obtain
   493	$\Id \ot M^{\Variable_1,\omega} M^{\Variable_5,\omega}
   494	\approx_{\sqrt{\eps_\omega}} -\Id \ot M^{\Variable_5,\omega} M^{\Variable_1,\omega}$,
   495	the anticommutation consequence for the second player, which is then
   496	averaged over $\omega$ with Jensen's inequality.  The corrected theorem needs
   497	in addition the defects $\Delta_1(\strategy_\omega), \Delta_5(\strategy_\omega)$.
   498	They are available from the lemma: item~7 states that, on average over
   499	anticommuting $\omega$, the first player's trace-postprocessed point
   500	measurement $\{P_a\}$ agrees with the second player's $\Variable_1$ measurement,
   501	$P_a \ot \Id \simeq_\eps \Id \ot M^{\Variable_1,\omega}_a$, and the lemma's
   502	final clause gives the same with the tensor factors interchanged; item~1
   503	states that the point measurements are consistent between the players,
   504	$P_a \ot \Id \simeq_\eps \Id \ot P_a$.  Two applications of the triangle
   505	inequality, after converting $\simeq_\eps$ to $\approx_\eps$ by the lemma's own
   506	final clause, give
   507	$M^{\Variable_1,\omega}_a \ot \Id \approx_\eps \Id \ot M^{\Variable_1,\omega}_a$
   508	on average over $\omega$, that is, $\E_\omega \Delta_1(\strategy_\omega)
   509	= O(\eps)$, and likewise for $\Variable_5$ with the $Z$-basis point
   510	measurement.  Applying the corrected theorem with $\delta_\omega =

511	\Delta_1(\strategy_\omega) + \Delta_5(\strategy_\omega)$ gives the
   512	anticommutation with error $\sqrt{\eps_\omega} + \sqrt{\delta_\omega}$, and
   513	Jensen's inequality bounds its average by
   514	$\sqrt{\E\eps_\omega} + \sqrt{\E\delta_\omega} = O(\sqrt\eps)$, which is the
   515	bound the source obtains.  The application thus goes through with one extra
   516	triangle inequality and no new input.
   517	
   518	The Lean side of the application confirms both halves of this.  The induced
   519	strategy \leanid{MIPStarRE.QPBT.ProjectiveSetting.msStrategyAt} is an
   520	arbitrary strategy of \leanid{MIPStarRE.QPBT.msGame} with separate local
   521	spaces for the two players, not a symmetric strategy, which is why the
   522	corrected theorem is stated for arbitrary strategies; and the two consistency
   523	inputs above are the statements
   524	\leanid{MIPStarRE.QPBT.win\_ms\_cons\_approx} (item~7, both orientations, in
   525	the $\approx$ form) and \leanid{MIPStarRE.QPBT.pointObs\_self\_consistent}
   526	(item~1, in observable form) of
   527	\doclink{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/WinImplications.lean}, from which the
   528	average defect of \leanid{MIPStarRE.QPBT.ProjectiveSetting.msStrategyAt} over
   529	anticommuting tuples is bounded by $O(\eps)$ by the same two triangle
   530	inequalities.  That derivation is part of the consumer packets
   531	(\ghissue{115} and its successors), not of the rigidity theorem.
   532	
   533	\section{Comparison with the blueprint and formalization}
   534	\label{sec:formal}
   535	
   536	The blueprint \cite{MIPStarREBlueprint} states \path{thm:ms-rigidity} in the
   537	corrected form of item~4 of Section~2, with the hypothesis \eqref{eq:defect}
   538	displayed and the source's unrestricted statement, its refutation, and the
   539	derivation above recorded in the proof and in the remark that follows the
   540	theorem.  The Lean declaration \leanid{MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists\_ms\_rigidity}
   541	carries the same statement: it quantifies over $\eps, \delta \ge 0$ and an
   542	arbitrary strategy of \leanid{MIPStarRE.QPBT.msGame} of value at least
   543	$1-\eps$ whose defects \leanid{MIPStarRE.QPBT.msVariableConsistencyDefect} at
   544	the cells $0$ and $4$ (the paper's $\Variable_1$ and $\Variable_5$) are at most
   545	$\delta$, and concludes the seven estimates of the source at scale
   546	$C(\sqrt\eps + \sqrt\delta)$ for one universal constant $C$, with the witness
   547	and distance definitions unchanged.  The statement-level \verb|\leanok| records
   548	that the Lean statement matches the blueprint statement; the proof is the
   549	tracked \verb|sorry| owned by \ghissue{105}, and no proof-level
   550	\verb|\leanok| is claimed.  Three sorry-free companions accompany it:
   551	\leanid{MIPStarRE.QPBT.msVariableConsistencyDefect\_eq\_zero\_of\_isConsistent}
   552	shows that a symmetric consistent strategy has zero defects;
   553	\leanid{MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists\_ms\_rigidity\_of\_symmetric\_consistent}
   554	derives from the theorem its specialization to that class, whose conclusion is
   555	the source's display; and
   556	\leanid{MIPStarRE.QPBT.MagicSquareRigidity.msVarObsA\_close\_msVarObsB}
   557	transfers the hypothesis to the dilated reflections.
   558	
   559	What remains for \ghissue{105} is the assembly of the corrected theorem from
   560	the chain: the approximate anticommutation and cross-commutation of the second
   561	logical pair, the reflections at the paper's $\Variable_2$ and $\Variable_4$,
   562	by the same solution-group computation; the joint swap-isometry extraction of
   563	the two EPR pairs from each player's two anticommuting pairs and from the
   564	cross-player agreement above, giving (\path{thm:ms-rigidity},~1) at scale
   565	$\sqrt\eps + \sqrt\delta$; the intertwining of each player's extracted qubit
   566	observables with $\sigma^X$ and $\sigma^Z$; and the post-isometry transfers,
   567	which already exist.  Nothing in this list needs symmetry, and nothing needs
   568	consistency beyond the two defects in the hypothesis.
   569	
   570	\section{Conclusion}
   571	
   572	The verdict is a theorem-level gap: the rigidity theorem for the Magic Square
   573	game is false as printed.  Its conclusion forces the two players' $\Variable_1$
   574	and $\Variable_5$ measurements to agree on the shared state, while the
   575	role-symmetric game never sends the same question to both players, and a
   576	perfect strategy that answers the two orientations on two independent
   577	maximally entangled copies violates the conclusion at $\eps = 0$; so does its
   578	symmetric player-role symmetrization, so symmetry alone does not repair the
   579	statement.  The adopted correction assumes that agreement, measured by the
   580	defect \eqref{eq:defect} at the two distinguished variables, and replaces
   581	$\sqrt\eps$ by $\sqrt\eps + \sqrt\delta$; symmetric consistent strategies are
   582	its case $\delta = 0$, both counterexamples have defect $1$, the source's
   583	application supplies the defect up to $O(\eps)$ from its own consistency
   584	subtests, and the cited one-way self-test proves the corrected statement.
   585	The blueprint and \leanid{MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists\_ms\_rigidity} now carry this
   586	form; its proof is the assembly tracked by \ghissue{105}.

    35	    {X Y Outcome iota : Type*}

    38	    [Fintype Outcome] [DecidableEq Outcome]

    43	        (fun x a => A (e x) a) (fun x a => B (e x) a) psi =

    45	  unfold consistencyDefect
    46	  simpa using avgOver_uniform_equiv e (fun x =>

    50	          (((A (e x) a) * (B (e x) b)).mulVec psi))).re)

    66	  apply avgOver_congr
    67	  intro x
    68	  let term : Alpha → Alpha → ℝ := fun a b =>

    76	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
